question: A sum of money increases to ₹7,500 after 5 years and ₹9,200 after 7 years respectively at the same rate of simple interest. Find the approximate rate of interest per annum.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SI for (7 − 5) = 2 years = ₹9,200 − ₹7,500 = ₹1,700.

SI for 1 year = 1700 ÷ 2 = ₹850.

Principal (P) = Amount after 5 years − SI for 5 years = 7500 − (850 × 5) = ₹3,250.

Rate % = (SI for 1 year ÷ P) × 100 = (850 ÷ 3250) × 100.

Rate % = 340 ÷ 13 ≈ 26.15% ≈ 26.2%.

**∴ The correct answer is 26.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Timeline of Amount Growth

**Given:**

Amount after 5 years (A₅) = ₹7,500

Amount after 7 years (A₇) = ₹9,200

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 2 years = A₇ − A₅ = 9200 − 7500 = ₹1,700

⇒ SI for 1 year = 1700 ÷ 2 = ₹850

⇒ SI for 5 years = 850 × 5 = ₹4,250

⇒ Principal (P) = A₅ − SI for 5 years = 7500 − 4250 = ₹3,250

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ P

⇒ R = (850 × 100) ÷ 3250

⇒ R = 85000 ÷ 3250 = 8500 ÷ 325 = 340 ÷ 13

⇒ R ≈ 26.1538% ≈ 26.2%

**∴ The correct answer is 26.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Amount Formula

The total amount after T years at rate R is given by A = P[1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on the same principal is D = P(R ÷ 100)².

Principal from Direct Amount Formula

If Amount A is known for time T and rate R, the Principal P = (100 × A) ÷ (100 + R × T).
